Row 78: CLAUDE.md tells a reader to check the raw-font rule by grepping UIFont.systemFont, and that returns ZERO. Swift's implicit-member form, .systemFont(ofSize, returns EIGHTEEN — sixteen in HostAppViewController and two in ManagedAppViewController, the two view controllers that host the Assist gate, at fixed 9-12pt. The screen that tells a worker why they were blocked does not grow at accessibility text sizes. dd55bca converted eight other view controllers on 2026-08-18 and skipped these two; SG-token adoption and adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory correlate 1:1 across every file that was converted. Row 58: SessionData.isExpired is `guard let expiresAt = expiresAt else { return false }` — a session that cannot say when it expires reads as NOT expired — and HostAppViewController:189 stacks a second permissive default on top. `stale` is a live posture input to the Assist gate, and nil is producible by a real auth path. Neither file is a frozen port, so golden rule 1 does not block the fix.

OPERATION 4 - row 58 is a DESIGN call, not a mechanical flip, and I am not making it from here. Do not simply invert the default: make absence explicit. A SessionData that cannot state an expiry should be distinguishable from one that never expires — e.g. an expiry policy of .expiresAt(Date) or .nonExpiring(justification:) — so isExpired has no ignorance branch at all. If you disagree with that shape, say so in the lane mail and pick your own; the requirement is that an unknown expiry stops reading as valid.
